title: Godot 4 Humanoid overwrites all bone rests (lack of importer setting documentation)
body:
### Tested versions

v4.4.1.stable.mono.official [49a5bc7b6]

### System information

Manjaro Linux - Godot v4.4.1.stable - Vulkan (Forward+)

### Issue description

When a model (used GLTF as a GLB in testing) is imported and has a bone map humanoid applied all bone orientations are lost. The shape of the rig does not change but all bones have mismatched rotations from the base rig. This breaks BoneAttachment3D and any code that could be built to rely on this information. A good example would be copying rotations between bones with the same orientations. This breaks because the orientations no longer match.
This implementation makes using a humanoid bone map completely impractical as it breaks rigs which may be made to use their orientations outside of animation (Ex: nodes attached via BoneAttachment3D)
I feel it would be better to make a humanoid system where the bones are not modified like this would be much better.

### Steps to reproduce

1) Export a rigged model from Blender as GLTF that is a humanoid (ideally with extra bones like a tail)
2) Add a humanoid bone map
3) Bone orientations no longer match even if they aren't used in the humanoid.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The test scene has two of the exact same model overlapping. One has a bone map, one doesn't. You can see the orientations are different.
[mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19612820/mrp.zip)
